contexts.title: Tallowmarket prep notes (candidate)
contexts.text:
PREP NOTES - Tallowmarket, Senior Backend Engineer (Payments & Ledger)
Last edited Sep 27. Private, just for me.

People
- Recruiter: Hollis Brandt. Screen was Sep 24, went fine, she was chatty.
- Hiring manager: Ruth Okonkwo-Sealy, leads Payments & Ledger. This round is with her.
- Imani Castellanos is only in the final values round, not this one.

What I learned from the recruiter screen and their engineering blog
- Harrow started in 2023 as one PostgreSQL database. Ledger entries are append-only and balances per grower account are materialized every 15 minutes.
- The real pain right now: the nightly settlement batch overran twice in August and missed the bank file cutoff, so grower payouts slipped a day. Hollis called this 'basically the reason this req exists'.
- They are moving refunds and chargebacks onto Temporal this quarter. Two services are already on it.
- Events from the order service into Harrow are consumed at-least-once. They dedupe with a processed_events table that Hollis said is 'getting huge'.
- The team is 6 engineers plus Ruth. Two of the engineers are mid-level and joined this year.

My angle for 'why this role' (my own words, don't read it out)
- Settlement is the part of Larkspur I actually liked. The reconciliation job took mismatches from 312 to 41 a month, and what stuck with me is that money bugs are nearly always ordering or duplicate-delivery bugs.
- I have run Temporal in production with Metronome and I know where it bites, which is exactly where they are heading with refunds.
- Dockhand's outbox is the same shape of problem as their processed_events growth.
- The load_events partitioning (vacuum from 4 hours to 35 minutes) is relevant if Harrow's entry table really heads toward 1.5 million a day.
- I want my next role to be one where I own a money-path service end to end, not a rewrite I hand off after launch.

Things NOT to claim
- I have not built a double-entry ledger. Say so plainly and talk about reconciliation instead.
- No Stripe Connect or Adyen. No PCI scope work.

Questions to ask Ruth
1. How is on-call split between Harrow and payouts?
2. Is the 02:00 batch owned by this team alone or shared with Finance?
3. What does L5 scope look like here compared with L4?
4. What would the first 90 days look like for this hire?

Logistics
Video call, 45 minutes, Thursday 10:30 Eastern. Have the Tern design doc summary open in another window. Water. Close Slack. Camera at eye level.

contexts.title: Quarrystone Logistics onsite checklist
contexts.text:
QUARRYSTONE LOGISTICS - onsite prep checklist (Oct 8)

Role: Staff Engineer, Warehouse Robotics Fleet.
Panel: Pradeep Ollivander (fleet control), Marguerite Sato (simulation), Kofi Ansah-Berg (engineering manager).

Their stack: C++ and Rust on the robots, a Python simulation harness, ROS 2, and a Scala scheduling service they are trying to retire.
Their product: about 1,200 autonomous pallet movers across 14 fulfillment centers. The main complaint in their job posts is deadlock between robots at aisle intersections.

Questions to ask them
- How do you recover a robot that loses localization mid-aisle?
- Who owns the scheduler rewrite, and is there a hard deadline?
- How much of the job is on the warehouse floor versus at a desk?
- What does the first month look like for a staff hire?

Directions: Building C, 2200 Ferrous Way. Check in with security at the front desk; they need a photo ID. Visitor parking is behind Building D, not in the loading area.
Bring: two printed copies of the robotics portfolio, laptop charger, a notebook.
Dress: they said jeans are fine, closed-toe shoes required for the floor tour.
Thank-you notes go to Kofi within 24 hours.

contexts.title: Self-review draft H1 2025 (Tobias V.)
contexts.text:
SELF-REVIEW DRAFT - H1 2025 (Tobias V.) - not final, numbers still being checked with Grace

Summary
First half was mostly Project Tern and the quoting performance work. Rate-quote p95 is now at 190 ms, down from 820 ms, and settlement mismatches keep trending down.

Impact
1. Rate-quote API: replaced the N+1 PostgreSQL queries with a batched loader and added a Redis cache keyed by lane ID with a 60-second TTL. p95 went from 820 ms to 210 ms on the March dashboard.
2. Dockhand: now handling roughly 3.2 million shipment status events a day through the transactional outbox, with zero duplicate writes found in the April audit.
3. Reconciliation: the nightly job has brought monthly settlement mismatches from 312 down to 44.
4. Tern: working group of 4 engineers and 1 QA analyst; two of the three Go services are in production, the third is planned for Q3.

Operational
- On the 5-person on-call rotation. Wrote 14 runbooks, plus 2 more in draft.
- Vacuum on load_events after partitioning: 35 minutes, down from about 4 hours.

Growth areas (for Grace)
- Write design docs earlier; the Tern doc came after the first service was already half built.
- Get better at saying no to side requests during launch weeks.

Open questions before I submit
- Do we quote the p95 from the March dashboard or from the June one? They disagree.
- Is the cache TTL 60 or 90 seconds in prod right now? Check the config.
- Confirm the Dockhand daily volume with the data team; my number may be from the peak week.
contexts.notes: Contradictions: rate-quote p95 is 190 ms in the summary but 210 ms in impact bullet 1 (resume says 190 ms); cache TTL 60 seconds here vs 90 seconds on the resume; Dockhand volume 3.2 million/day here vs 2.3 million on the resume; mismatches 312 to 44 here vs 312 to 41 on the resume; on-call rotation 5-person here vs 6-person on the resume; the doc itself flags the March vs June dashboard disagreement.
